summary: Modern data platforms have rapidly integrated AI/ML capabilities directly into their engines, with vector search becoming a defining enterprise requirement — ACI Infotech projects 75% of enterprise AI applications will depend on vector search by 2026, and adoption grew 377% year over year (SG Analytics). Approaches range from fully managed in-database LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex AI, BigQuery ML) to native vector indexing (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks Vector Search) and extension-based vector support (PostgreSQL/Aurora pgvector). The trend is toward making data 'AI-ready by design,' with platforms like Snowflake embedding Postgres, graph (Apache AGE), and agentic AI (AI CoWork, reaching GA in June 2026) natively.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, Snowflake Intelligence, AI CoWork)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) via SQL/Python functions for summarization, translation, sentiment, and RAG. As of January 2026 Snowflake reported 9,100+ Cortex AI accounts, and Snowflake Intelligence crossed 2,500 accounts within three months (reported May 2026). The agentic AI CoWork and Adaptive Compute reached general availability in June 2026. February 2026 announcements made data 'AI-ready by design' with Snowflake Postgres running natively in the AI Data Cloud, including Apache AGE for graph/openCypher queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports the VECTOR data type with VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE/VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY functions, and Cortex Search provides managed hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval directly in the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Deeply integrated — hosted LLMs callable via Cortex functions, plus Cortex Analyst (text-to-SQL), Cortex Search, and agentic workflows through Snowflake Intelligence and AI CoWork.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based (credits). Cortex LLM functions billed per token processed; vector/embedding and Cortex Search billed on compute and storage. No separate license required beyond standard Snowflake consumption.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows creating and running ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, deep models) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call Gemini and other foundation models directly from SQL via remote models for generation, embeddings, and multimodal analysis, keeping data in place without movement.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF and TreeAH), enabling similarity search directly in SQL over embeddings generated via ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Vertex AI remote models — Gemini and embedding models invoked through SQL functions (ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING).
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML priced on bytes processed for queries plus model creation/inference costs; Vertex AI remote model calls billed separately per the underlying foundation model. On-demand and capacity (slot) pricing options available.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search (L2, cosine, inner product) with HNSW and IVFFlat indexing to PostgreSQL. pgai (from Timescale) adds in-database embedding generation and LLM calls (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, etc.) via SQL, plus pgvectorscale for scalable indexing. Together they turn Postgres into a capable RAG and vector platform within the open-source ecosystem.
databases.vector_search_notes: Extension-based, not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search requires installing the third-party pgvector (and optionally pgvectorscale/pgai) extensions; it is not a built-in engine feature.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which enables embedding generation and LLM API calls from SQL; not part of core PostgreSQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs depend on hosting (self-managed or managed provider) plus any external LLM API usage incurred by pgai calls.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (SageMaker, Bedrock & Comprehend integration)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you call ML models from SQL by integrating Aurora (MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible) with Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock (foundation models/LLMs), and Amazon Comprehend. This enables predictions, sentiment analysis, and generative AI inference directly in SQL queries without managing custom integration code.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora PostgreSQL supports vector search only through the pgvector extension, which is a third-party extension rather than a built-in Aurora engine feature; Aurora MySQL does not provide native vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — via Amazon Bedrock integration callable from SQL, plus SageMaker and Comprehend for custom and NLP models.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I/O pricing; ML inference incurs separate charges from SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend based on usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML allows data analysts and warehouse users to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL, automatically leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database inference and integration with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI, enabling large-scale analytical ML and LLM calls directly in the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native in the core engine historically; Redshift has added support for vector data handling and integrates with external vector/embedding workflows, but it is not positioned as a native built-in vector search database. Treat vector search as not a first-class native feature.
databases.llm_integration: Yes — integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker, invokable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift cluster/serverless compute pricing; model training via SageMaker and LLM inference via Bedrock billed separately based on usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end generative AI tooling — foundation model fine-tuning, model serving, RAG, agent frameworks, and evaluation — on the lakehouse. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with Unity Catalog, offering automatic embedding sync from Delta tables and governed similarity search for RAG applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, fully managed vector index service with automatic sync from Delta tables and governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Deep — Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts foundation models and external LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic), with agent, RAG, and fine-tuning frameworks native to the platform.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based (DBUs) for compute, model serving, and Vector Search endpoints; foundation model inference billed per token or via provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search + Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search provides native vector similarity search integrated with MongoDB's document model, enabling semantic search and RAG over operational data without a separate vector store. It supports approximate nearest neighbor search (HNSW), hybrid search combining vector and full-text, and integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and major LLM providers.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas, using $vectorSearch aggregation stage with HNSW indexing directly on documents — no separate database required.
databases.llm_integration: Via integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and embedding/LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, AWS Bedrock); embeddings stored alongside documents for RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Included in Atlas cluster pricing; dedicated Search Nodes can be provisioned separately to scale vector workloads. Costs scale with cluster tier, storage, and search node resources.
